problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta +1}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }?$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1} & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-({tan}^{2}⁡x+1)} \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{sec}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can further simplify our expression, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{sec}^{2}⁡x} & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x({sec}^{2}⁡x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡x}}{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡x}({sec}^{2}⁡x-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x)-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x} \\  & ={(\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x})}^{2} \\  & ={cot}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1}={cot}^{2}⁡x.
$$
